description: ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT expr) drops repeated values, with or without WITHIN GROUP, while a plain ARRAY_AGG keeps them; numeric duplicates compare by value so 1 and 1.0 are one element. SQL NULLs are skipped entirely - the loader idiom ARRAY_AGG(IFF(cond, obj, NULL)) must yield [] when no row qualifies, not [null] - and that holds under WITHIN GROUP ordering too. Converted 1:1 from functions/ArrayAggDistinctTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach fixture is inlined per test and the array cells are read through TO_JSON so the assertion is on the array's JSON text rather than on a transport's own rendering of an ARRAY cell.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE labels (grp INTEGER, tag VARCHAR)
SELECT TO_JSON(ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT tag) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY tag)) FROM labels WHERE grp = 1 GROUP BY grp
CREATE TABLE labels (grp INTEGER, tag VARCHAR)
SELECT ARRAY_SIZE(ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT tag)) FROM labels WHERE grp = 1 GROUP BY grp
CREATE TABLE labels (grp INTEGER, tag VARCHAR)
SELECT ARRAY_SIZE(ARRAY_AGG(tag)) FROM labels WHERE grp = 1 GROUP BY grp
CREATE TABLE nulled (grp INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO nulled VALUES (1, NULL), (1, NULL), (2, 'a'), (2, NULL)
SELECT TO_JSON(ARRAY_AGG(v)) FROM nulled WHERE grp = 1 GROUP BY grp
SELECT TO_JSON(ARRAY_AGG(v)) FROM nulled WHERE grp = 2 GROUP BY grp
CREATE TABLE nulled2 (v VARCHAR, k INTEGER)
SELECT TO_JSON(ARRAY_AGG(v) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY k)) FROM nulled2
